newsitem.title: UK: BA to offer 10 pound Concorde flights.
newsitem.headline: BA to offer 10 pound Concorde flights.

text.p: British Airways will sell tickets for flights on its supersonic Concorde for only 10 pounds ($16.40) to mark the 10th anniversary of its privatisation, the airline said in a statement on Monday.

People can buy up to two return tickets between London's Heathrow airport and New York for 10 pounds each, 5,400 pounds ($8,857) below the normal fare, by calling the main British Airways telephone sales office at 2200 GMT on Tuesday.
Ten seats on every return Concorde flight from London to New York for the 10 days after February 12 will be sold.
British Airways will also offer 100 free Concorde tickets to staff who can give the best reason why they and a friend deserve a trip to New York, the statement said.

"As we owe the success of British Airways to so many people over the past 10 years we wanted to give everybody a chance to join our birthday celebrations," said Bob Ayling, the airline's chief executive.

British Airways was privatised on February 11, 1987. Almost 300 million people have flown with the airline, which has nearly doubled the size of its fleet in the last 10 years to 295. ($1=.6097 Pound)
